question: Prithviraja III defeated an Afghan ruler named ______ in 1191.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sultan Muhammad Ghori.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prithviraj III (Prithviraja Chauhan), the Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler of Ajmer and Delhi, defeated the Ghurid ruler Muhammad of Ghor (Muhammad Ghori) in the First Battle of Tarain (Taraori) in 1191 CE. (पृथ्वीराज तृतीय — मुहम्मद गौरी)

 

• After his defeat, Ghori regrouped and returned the following year, decisively defeating Prithviraj III in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE), which marked the beginning of Muslim rule in northern India.

 

• Prithviraj III belonged to the Chahamana (Chauhan) dynasty and is remembered in Indian tradition through the epic poem Prithviraj Raso, composed by his court poet Chand Bardai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad Ghori (Muizuddin Muhammad bin Sam) laid the foundation of Muslim rule in India; after his death (1206), his slave-general Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk/Slave Dynasty).

 

NOTE

 

• Sultan Mahmud (Option 1): Refers to Mahmud of Ghazni, who raided India (including Somnath, 1025) in the early 11th century, much earlier than 1191.

 

• Muhammad Ibn Abbas (Option 2): Not a historical Afghan ruler associated with this battle; a distractor name.

 

• Muhammad Ibn Suri (Option 3): Not the ruler who fought Prithviraj III at Tarain; a distractor name.

question: Sharmila Biswas, who was awarded the ‘Best Choreography Award’ in 1998 by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, represents which of the following classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sharmila Biswas is a renowned exponent, choreographer and teacher of Odissi, a classical dance form of Odisha. (शर्मिला विश्वास — ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• She trained under the legendary Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and is known for her innovative group choreography, blending traditional Odissi vocabulary with contemporary themes.

 

• She was conferred the 'Best Choreography Award' in 1998 by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, and has also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to Odissi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha and is characterised by the tribhangi (three-bend) posture and chowk stance; other noted Odissi exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, and Madhavi Mudgal.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 1): Classical dance of Manipur, associated with exponents like the Jhaveri sisters and Guru Bipin Singh.

 

• Kathakali (Option 3): Classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

 

• Kathak (Option 4): Classical dance form of North India, associated with exponents like Birju Maharaj.

question: The Paralympics Games - 2024 will be hosted by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2024 Summer Paralympic Games were held in Paris, France, from 28 August to 8 September 2024. (पेरिस पैरालंपिक 2024 — फ्रांस)

 

• Paris hosted the Paralympics for the first time, following the Summer Olympics 2024 also held in the same city.

 

• India put up its best-ever Paralympic performance at the Paris 2024 Games, winning a total of 29 medals (7 gold, 9 silver, 13 bronze).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2020 Summer Paralympics (postponed to 2021 due to COVID-19) were held in Tokyo, Japan; the next edition, the 2028 Paralympics, is scheduled for Los Angeles, USA.

 

NOTE

 

• USA (Option 1): Not the 2024 host; Los Angeles will host the Paralympics in 2028.

 

• China (Option 2): Beijing hosted the 2022 Winter Paralympics, not the 2024 Summer Games.

 

• Spain (Option 3): Has not hosted a recent edition of the Paralympic Games.

question: The women of which tribe perform the traditional folk dance called Chakri?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanjar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chakri is a traditional folk dance performed by the women of the Kanjar tribe, a community found mainly in Madhya Pradesh. (चकरी नृत्य — कंजर जनजाति)

 

• The dance is performed in a circular pattern, with dancers whirling rapidly to the beat of folk instruments, and is traditionally associated with festive and social occasions of the community.

 

• The Kanjar are among the many tribal/folk communities of Madhya Pradesh, a state noted for its rich diversity of tribal folk dances such as Saila, Karma, Gaur, and Bhagoria.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh, often called the 'heart of India', has one of the largest tribal populations in the country, including Gond, Bhil, Baiga, Korku, and Kanjar communities.

 

NOTE

 

• Kaul (Option 1): Not the tribe associated with the Chakri dance.

 

• Gond (Option 3): A major tribal group of central India, known for dances like Karma and Saila, not Chakri.

 

• Bharia (Option 4): A tribal community of Madhya Pradesh (Patalkot region), not associated with the Chakri dance.

question: Which of the following terms is NOT included in the Preamble of Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Federalism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Preamble to the Indian Constitution declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and secures to its citizens Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity. (प्रस्तावना — संप्रभु, समाजवादी, पंथनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य)

 

• The word 'Federalism' does not appear anywhere in the text of the Preamble, even though India's constitutional structure is, in practice, federal in nature (with a strong unitary bias).

 

• The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976; all the other terms (Sovereign, Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity) were part of the original 1950 Preamble.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble also mentions the objectives of Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and Equality of status and of opportunity.

 

• The Preamble was described by N.A. Palkhivala as the 'identity card of the Constitution', and its basic features were held to be unamendable in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

 

NOTE

 

• Sovereign (Option 1): Explicitly present in the Preamble, denoting India's freedom from external control.

 

• Justice (Option 2): Explicitly present in the Preamble, covering social, economic and political justice.

 

• Fraternity (Option 3): Explicitly present in the Preamble, promoting the dignity of the individual and unity/integrity of the nation.

question: The State Finance Commission is appointed every ____ years by the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5, state government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 243-I of the Constitution, the Governor of a State (the constitutional head of the state government) is required to constitute a State Finance Commission at the expiry of every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities. (राज्य वित्त आयोग — 5 वर्ष, राज्य सरकार)

 

• This provision was inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (for Panchayats) and extended to Municipalities by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (Article 243-Y).

 

• The State Finance Commission recommends the distribution of taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the state and local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities), and the grants-in-aid to be given to them from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This is distinct from the Finance Commission (constituted by the President under Article 280, also every 5 years) which deals with the distribution of resources between the Union and the states.

 

NOTE

 

• 5, central government (Option 2): Incorrect authority — the State Finance Commission is constituted by the state (Governor), not the Union/central government.

 

• 2.5, state government (Option 3): Incorrect periodicity — the correct interval is 5 years, not 2.5 years.

 

• 2.5, central government (Option 4): Incorrect on both counts — neither the periodicity nor the constituting authority is correct.

question: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 amends the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 to empower the central government to specify a _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is carbon credit trading scheme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 amends the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, empowering the central government to specify and establish a carbon credit trading scheme in India. (ऊर्जा संरक्षण संशोधन विधेयक 2022 — कार्बन क्रेडिट व्यापार योजना)

 

• The Bill provides the legal framework for a domestic carbon market, enabling entities to trade carbon credit certificates and mandates the use of non-fossil energy sources, including green hydrogen, biomass, and ethanol.

 

• It also empowers the government to set a mandatory minimum consumption of non-fossil sources by industries, and mandates energy efficiency/conservation standards for large residential and commercial buildings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 2022, giving legislative backing to India's commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070.

 

NOTE

 

• Coal based station (Option 2): Not a subject matter of this amendment, which focuses on energy efficiency and carbon trading.

 

• Coastal regulation scheme (Option 3): Relates to environmental regulation of coastal areas under separate CRZ notifications, not this Act.

 

• Eco-sensitive zone (Option 4): Notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, unrelated to the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill.

question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill 2022 seeks to unify the how many municipal corporations into a single one?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022 unified the three existing municipal corporations of Delhi — the North, South, and East Delhi Municipal Corporations — into a single Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD). (दिल्ली नगर निगम संशोधन विधेयक 2022 — तीन निगमों का एकीकरण)

 

• The three corporations had originally been created by trifurcating the unified Municipal Corporation of Delhi in 2011 (via a 2011 amendment to the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957) to improve civic administration.

 

• The 2022 Bill reversed this trifurcation, citing financial unviability and resource imbalance among the three corporations, and re-established a unified MCD with effect from May 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Following unification, elections for the unified MCD were held in December 2022, with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) winning a majority.

 

NOTE

 

• Four, Two, Five (Options 1, 3, 4): Incorrect — Delhi had exactly three municipal corporations (North, South, East) prior to the 2022 unification.

question: What is the role of ribosomes of a polysome?
option_2: The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
option_3: The ribosomes of a polysome translate the rRNA into proteins.
option_4: The ribosomes of a monosome translate the rRNA into proteins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A polysome (polyribosome) is a cluster of multiple ribosomes simultaneously attached to and moving along a single messenger RNA (mRNA) molecule during translation. (पॉलिसोम — mRNA का प्रोटीन में अनुवाद)

 

• Each ribosome in the chain independently reads the same mRNA strand and synthesises a separate copy of the encoded polypeptide (protein), making protein synthesis highly efficient.

 

• Ribosomes are the cell organelles responsible for protein synthesis; they are composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins, and are found either free in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ribosomes have two subunits — a large subunit and a small subunit — which come together on the mRNA to carry out translation with the help of tRNA (transfer RNA), which brings amino acids to the ribosome.

 

NOTE

 

• The ribosomes synthesise the fats (Option 1): Incorrect — fats are synthesised in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, not by ribosomes.

 

• The ribosomes of a polysome translate the rRNA into proteins (Option 3): Incorrect — ribosomes translate mRNA, not rRNA; rRNA is a structural/functional component of the ribosome itself.

 

• The ribosomes of a monosome translate the rRNA into proteins (Option 4): Incorrect on two counts — the question concerns a polysome, not a monosome, and ribosomes translate mRNA, not rRNA.

question: Which type of tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in the economy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Proportional income tax.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An automatic stabiliser is a fiscal mechanism that automatically moderates fluctuations in national income without any deliberate government action. (स्वचालित स्थिरक — आय कर)

 

• Income tax acts as a classic automatic stabiliser: as national income rises during a boom, tax collections rise (moderating demand), and as income falls during a slowdown, tax collections fall automatically, cushioning the fall in disposable income and aggregate demand.

 

• Among the given options, only income tax (proportional income tax) is directly and automatically linked to the level of income/output in the economy, making it the operative automatic stabiliser.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common automatic stabilisers in an economy include unemployment allowances/benefits and corporate profit taxes, both of which move inversely/directly with the business cycle without requiring fresh legislation.

 

NOTE

 

• Professional tax (Option 1): A fixed/slab-based tax levied by state governments on income from a profession, not linked automatically to overall economic fluctuations.

 

• Wealth tax (Option 2): Levied on the net wealth of an assessee (now abolished in India); it is not primarily a business-cycle stabiliser.

 

• Capital gains tax (Option 3): Levied on gains from the sale of capital assets; it is transaction-specific rather than a broad-based automatic stabiliser of aggregate income.

question: The world’s largest river lies in which of the following continent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South America.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Amazon River, widely regarded as the world's largest river by discharge/volume of water (and among the longest, rivalling the Nile), flows through South America. (अमेजन नदी — दक्षिण अमेरिका)

 

• The Amazon originates in the Peruvian Andes and flows eastward through Peru, Colombia, and Brazil before draining into the Atlantic Ocean, carrying roughly one-fifth of the world's total river flow into the ocean.

 

• The Amazon Basin, covering about 40% of South America, hosts the Amazon Rainforest, the largest tropical rainforest on Earth, often called the 'lungs of the planet'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nile River (Africa) is generally considered the longest river in the world by length, while the Amazon is the largest by discharge and, by some recent measurements, also the longest.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 2): Its largest river system, the Murray-Darling, is far smaller than the Amazon.

 

• Africa (Option 3): Home to the Nile, the longest river by length, but not the largest by volume.

 

• North America (Option 4): Its largest river, the Mississippi-Missouri, is much smaller than the Amazon in both length and discharge.

question: In which of the following months is Gokulashtami celebrated every year as per Hindu tradition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhadrapada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gokulashtami, also known as Janmashtami, marks the birth of Lord Krishna and is celebrated on the Ashtami (eighth day) of the Krishna Paksha in the Hindu month of Bhadrapada. (गोकुलाष्टमी/जन्माष्टमी — भाद्रपद मास)

 

• The Bhadrapada month typically corresponds to August-September in the Gregorian calendar, and the festival is celebrated with fasting, devotional singing (bhajans/kirtans), and the enactment of Krishna's childhood pastimes (Raslila).

 

• Celebrations include the famous Dahi Handi tradition (breaking a pot of curd/butter), especially prominent in Maharashtra, symbolising Krishna's playful theft of butter as a child.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major pilgrimage centres for Janmashtami celebrations include Mathura and Vrindavan in Uttar Pradesh, believed to be Krishna's birthplace and childhood home respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Vaishakh (Option 1): Falls in April-May; associated with festivals like Akshaya Tritiya and Buddha Purnima, not Gokulashtami.

 

• Asadha (Option 3): Falls in June-July; associated with the Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, not Gokulashtami.

 

• Chaitra (Option 4): Falls in March-April; marks the Hindu New Year and Ram Navami, not Gokulashtami.

question: Which of the following is NOT a method of measuring national income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intermediate goods method.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National income in India is conventionally measured using three standard methods: the Product (Value Added/Output) method, the Income method, and the Expenditure method. (राष्ट्रीय आय मापन — उत्पाद, आय, व्यय विधि)

 

• The Product method sums the value added by all producing units (avoiding double counting by excluding the value of intermediate goods); the Income method sums the incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) earned by factors of production; the Expenditure method sums total spending on final goods and services.

 

• There is no separate 'Intermediate goods method' for measuring national income — in fact, the value of intermediate goods is specifically excluded in the product method to avoid double counting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, national income estimates are compiled and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

NOTE

 

• Expenditure method (Option 2): A valid, recognised method of measuring national income.

 

• Income method (Option 3): A valid, recognised method of measuring national income.

 

• Product method (Option 4): A valid, recognised method of measuring national income.

question: Sambhar Lake is situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sambhar Lake, India's largest inland saltwater lake, is located in Rajasthan, spread across the districts of Jaipur, Ajmer and Nagaur. (साम्भर झील — राजस्थान)

 

• It is a major source of salt production in India, contributing a significant share of the country's salt output, and has been mined for salt for centuries.

 

• The lake is designated as a Ramsar site (Wetland of International Importance) and serves as an important habitat for migratory birds, notably flamingos.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable salt lakes of Rajasthan include Didwana Lake and Pachpadra Lake, both known for salt extraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Not the location of Sambhar Lake; known instead for backwaters like Vembanad Lake.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Not the location of Sambhar Lake.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Not the location of Sambhar Lake.

question: Which of the following waterways separates India from Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palk Strait.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Palk Strait separates Rameswaram Island (Tamil Nadu, India) from Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal to the Palk Bay. (पाक जलडमरूमध्य — भारत और श्रीलंका)

 

• Further south, the Gulf of Mannar also lies between India and Sri Lanka, and the mythical/geological chain of shoals known as Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu) links the two across the Palk Strait region.

 

• The Palk Strait is named after Robert Palk, a former British Governor of Madras.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands, while the Eight Degree Channel separates the Lakshadweep and Maldives island groups.

 

NOTE

 

• Arabian Sea (Option 1): Lies to the west of the Indian peninsula; does not separate India from Sri Lanka.

 

• Bay of Bengal (Option 2): Lies to the east of the Indian peninsula; a larger water body of which the Palk Strait region is a part, but not the specific waterway separating the two countries.

 

• Andaman Sea (Option 3): Lies east of the Andaman Islands, near Myanmar/Thailand; unrelated to the India-Sri Lanka boundary.

question: Which of the following is the highest gravity dam in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhakra Dam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bhakra Dam, built across the Sutlej River in Himachal Pradesh (on the border with Punjab), is the highest gravity dam in India, standing about 226 metres (740 feet) tall. (भाखड़ा बांध — सबसे ऊँचा ग्रेविटी बांध)

 

• It forms the reservoir known as Gobind Sagar Lake, one of the largest man-made lakes in India, and is a key part of the Bhakra-Nangal Project, providing irrigation and hydroelectric power to Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.

 

• A gravity dam relies primarily on the sheer weight of its own construction material to resist the horizontal pressure of water, distinguishing it from arch or buttress dams.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's tallest dam overall is the Tehri Dam (an earthfill/embankment dam on the Bhagirathi River, Uttarakhand), which is taller than Bhakra but is not classified as a gravity dam.

 

NOTE

 

• Hirakund Dam (Option 1): Built on the Mahanadi River, Odisha; notable for being one of the longest dams in the world, not the highest gravity dam.

 

• Sardar Sarovar Dam (Option 3): Built on the Narmada River, Gujarat; a major gravity dam but shorter than Bhakra.

 

• Mettur Dam (Option 4): Built on the Kaveri River, Tamil Nadu; not the highest gravity dam in India.

question: Identify the chemical formula of ammonium hydroxide.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NH4OH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ammonium hydroxide has the chemical formula NH4OH, formed when ammonia gas (NH3) dissolves in water, and is commonly known as 'liquor ammonia' or aqueous ammonia. (अमोनियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड — NH4OH)

 

• It is a weak base, widely used as a household cleaning agent, and in industrial processes such as the manufacture of fertilisers, textiles, and in laboratories as a reagent.

 

• The reaction of formation is: NH3 + H2O → NH4OH, where the ammonium ion (NH4+) combines with the hydroxide ion (OH−).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ammonium hydroxide is also used in the food industry as a pH control/leavening agent and in the production of rayon and other synthetic fibres.

 

NOTE

 

• NH4O2 (Option 2): Not a real/valid chemical formula for ammonium hydroxide.

 

• NH3O (Option 3): Not the correct formula; does not correctly represent the ammonium and hydroxide groups.

 

• NH2OH (Option 4): This is the formula for hydroxylamine, a different compound, not ammonium hydroxide.

question: Which of the following sites of Harappan civilization is located near Bolan Pass?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mehrgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mehrgarh, one of the earliest and most important Neolithic/Chalcolithic sites associated with the roots of the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilisation, is located near the Bolan Pass in present-day Balochistan, Pakistan. (मेहरगढ़ — बोलान दर्रा)

 

• Excavated primarily by French archaeologist Jean-Francois Jarrige, Mehrgarh provides evidence of early farming, animal domestication, and pottery, and is considered a precursor to the mature Harappan civilisation.

 

• The Bolan Pass, situated in the Toba Kakar mountain range, historically served as an important trade and migration route connecting the Indus plains with the Iranian plateau/Central Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mehrgarh is often described as providing the 'missing link' between the earliest neolithic settlements of the region and the fully developed urban Harappan civilisation of sites like Mohenjodaro and Harappa.

 

NOTE

 

• Chirand (Option 2): A Neolithic site in Bihar (on the Ganga), not near the Bolan Pass.

 

• Gufkral (Option 3): A Neolithic site in Jammu and Kashmir, not near the Bolan Pass.

 

• Koldihwa (Option 4): A Neolithic site in Uttar Pradesh, known for early rice cultivation evidence, not near the Bolan Pass.

question: How much percentage of nitrogen is present in the atmosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 78%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitrogen (N2) is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, constituting approximately 78% by volume. (वायुमंडल में नाइट्रोजन — 78%)

 

• It is followed by Oxygen (O2) at about 21%, and the remaining roughly 1% is composed of trace gases like argon, carbon dioxide, neon, helium, and water vapour.

 

• Nitrogen is largely chemically inert in its molecular form and plays a vital role in the nitrogen cycle, being converted into usable forms for plants via processes like nitrogen fixation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The atmosphere is broadly divided into layers — Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, and Exosphere — with the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful UV radiation, located within the Stratosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• 89%, 67%, 71% (Options 2, 3, 4): All incorrect figures; none represents the actual atmospheric composition of nitrogen, which is approximately 78%.

question: Partition of Bengal held in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Partition of Bengal was announced and implemented in 1905 by the then Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon, officially citing administrative convenience but widely seen as a move to weaken the nationalist movement by dividing Bengal along religious lines. (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905, लॉर्ड कर्जन)

 

• The partition divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam (Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority), and it took effect on 16 October 1905.

 

• It triggered the Swadeshi Movement and widespread protests, ultimately leading to the annulment of the partition in 1911 during the reign of King George V, announced at the Delhi Durbar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Swadeshi Movement promoted the boycott of British goods and the use of indigenous (swadeshi) products, and is considered a major turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, marking a shift toward mass mobilisation.

 

NOTE

 

• 1901, 1903, 1907 (Options 1, 2, 4): Incorrect years — the Partition of Bengal was formally implemented in 1905.

question: In which year was India House established by Shyamji Verma?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India House was established in 1905 in London (Highgate) by the revolutionary nationalist Shyamji Krishna Varma. (इंडिया हाउस — श्यामजी कृष्ण वर्मा, 1905)

 

• It served as a hostel for Indian students and quickly became a hub of revolutionary nationalist activity and radical political thought among Indians studying in Britain.

 

• Prominent revolutionaries associated with India House included Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (V.D. Savarkar), Madan Lal Dhingra, and Lala Hardayal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shyamji Krishna Varma also founded 'The Indian Sociologist', a monthly journal, and established the Indian Home Rule Society to promote the cause of Indian self-rule.

 

NOTE

 

• 1899, 1902, 1909 (Options 2, 3, 4): Incorrect years — India House was established in 1905.

question: In September 2022, which High Court has declared the “Duare Ration” scheme as illegal and against the National Food Security Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, the Calcutta High Court declared the West Bengal government's 'Duare Ration' (door-step ration delivery) scheme to be illegal, holding it to be against the provisions of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. (दुआरे राशन योजना — कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय)

 

• The scheme, launched by the West Bengal government, aimed to deliver subsidised food grains directly to beneficiaries' doorsteps instead of through Fair Price Shops (FPS).

 

• The court held that the scheme's mode of implementation departed from the statutory framework of ration distribution laid down under the NFSA and the Public Distribution System.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

question: Which country beat India in the men's hockey semi-final event at Tokyo Olympics, 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Belgium.

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), the Indian men's hockey team was defeated by Belgium in the semi-final, by a scoreline of 5-2. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक हॉकी — बेल्जियम से हार)

 

• Belgium went on to win the gold medal, defeating Australia in the final, while India defeated Germany 5-4 in the bronze medal match, ending a 41-year wait for an Olympic hockey medal for India (last medal being gold in 1980, Moscow).

 

• The Indian team was captained by Manpreet Singh, and goalkeeper P.R. Sreejesh played a key role in the bronze-medal-winning campaign.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's men's hockey team went on to win the bronze medal again at the 2024 Paris Olympics, defeating Spain in the bronze medal match.

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 1): India defeated Germany in the bronze medal match, not the semi-final.

 

• Pakistan (Option 2): Did not qualify for the Tokyo Olympics 2020 hockey event.

 

• Australia (Option 4): India played Australia in the quarter-final, defeating them 3-1, not the semi-final.

question: According to census 2011, the literacy rate of India is ______.

question: With which instrument is Ustad Sultan Khan associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarangi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Sultan Khan was a renowned Indian classical musician celebrated for his mastery of the Sarangi, a bowed, short-necked string instrument. (उस्ताद सुल्तान खान — सारंगी)

 

• Belonging to the Sikar gharana of Rajasthan, he was one of India's foremost Sarangi players, known for both solo classical performances and collaborations in film and fusion music (including the group Tabla Beat Science).

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2010) and was also a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, in recognition of his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sarangi is often described as the instrument that most closely mimics the tonal quality of the human voice, and is traditionally used to accompany vocal performances in Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Sitar (Option 1): A plucked string instrument famously associated with maestros like Pandit Ravi Shankar, not Ustad Sultan Khan.

 

• Sarod (Option 2): A plucked string instrument associated with maestros like Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, not Ustad Sultan Khan.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): A percussion instrument associated with maestros like Ustad Zakir Hussain, not Ustad Sultan Khan.
